Your play is close to your rating overall: you scored 48% against 49% expected [F1], and you made about as many blunders as similar-rated players would in your positions (0.99 times expected [F2]). The clearest thing to fix is missing discovered attacks.

## Biggest weaknesses

**1. Missing discovered attacks (a pattern).** When you blundered, the better move was a discovered attack 17 times, against 4 for your opponents [F22]. That is 4.25 times their rate, and it still holds after correcting for multiple comparisons [F22]. For example, you played 29.Bd7 and lost 86 win%, when the engine preferred Bf5 (https://www.chess.com/game/live/187005539854) [F23]. A related trend is worth watching but not yet confirmed: the better move was a hanging piece 28 times, against 16 for your opponents [F19]. One case is 43...Kh7, where Qxf4+ was available [F20].
*What to do:* before every move, look for any piece of yours sitting in front of your own rook, bishop or queen. Drill https://lichess.org/training/discoveredAttack [F24].

**2. Queen's Pawn Opening as White (possible weakness).** You scored 27% against 47% expected over 11 games [F7]. The median eval after move 12 was +0.0 [F13], so you get no advantage from the opening.
*What to do:* pick one concrete setup, such as the London, and learn its typical middlegame plans.

**3. Englund Gambit as Black (possible weakness).** You scored 21% against 49% expected over 7 games [F8], with a median eval of -0.4 after move 12 [F14]. The sample is small, so treat this as a warning sign rather than a firm conclusion. The same goes for the Pirc as White: 4 games, 0% scored [F6].
*What to do:* think about swapping the Englund for a sounder defence.

## What's working

- **Clock management in the middle zone.** With 10-30% of your clock left, you blundered only 0.74 times as often as expected, and the interval of 0.59 to 0.92 excludes 1 [F4]. Even under 10% you didn't blunder more than expected [F3].
- **Phase-by-phase play is even with your opponents.** In the endgame you blundered on 3.4% of moves against their 3.5% [F11].

## Training plan

- Do discovered-attack puzzles every day [F24], plus hanging-piece puzzles a few times a week (https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece) [F21].
- Use the most time when you have plenty of clock. Your blunder rate with over 30% left was 1.06 times expected [F5], so take a full blunder check before committing to a move.
- Do middlegame puzzle sets to sharpen your calculation (https://lichess.org/training/middlegame) [F28].
- Build a short repertoire file for the Queen's Pawn as White and a replacement for the Englund, then review your losses in those openings.
- Replay https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801649660 and find Qxf4+ yourself [F15].
